# Policy reference

The gate (`fleetgate.policy.Policy`) is a pure function of the proposal, the fleet state and the policy history. It is default-deny: a proposal is only allowed if every rule below passes. The first rule that fires decides, and every verdict carries a machine-readable reason code. Approval is asked only after every hard limit passed, so **approval can never override a DENY**. An exception while evaluating fails closed (`DENY_INTERNAL_ERROR`).

## Evaluation order

|  # | rule            | fires when                                                                                                              | code                        |
|---:|:----------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:----------------------------|
|  1 | unknown runbook | exact string match against the catalogue (no trim, case-fold or Unicode normalisation)                                  | `DENY_UNKNOWN_RUNBOOK`      |
|  2 | unknown host    | host id must exist in the fleet                                                                                         | `DENY_UNKNOWN_HOST`         |
|  3 | deny-list       | runbook is on the policy's deny_list                                                                                    | `DENY_LISTED_RUNBOOK`       |
|  4 | change freeze   | tier not in the active freeze window's allow_tiers (a maintenance window re-opens DISRUPTIVE work on unprotected hosts) | `DENY_FREEZE_WINDOW`        |
|  5 | preconditions   | every precondition of the runbook must hold right now                                                                   | `DENY_PRECONDITION_FAILED`  |
|  6 | cooldown        | same runbook on the same host within cooldown_ticks                                                                     | `DENY_COOLDOWN`             |
|  7 | tick budget     | max_actions_per_tick already executed this tick                                                                         | `DENY_TICK_BUDGET`          |
|  8 | rate limit      | rate_limits[runbook]: max executions per window                                                                         | `DENY_RATE_LIMIT`           |
|  9 | quotas          | per-role and per-datacenter action counts per window                                                                    | `DENY_QUOTA_ROLE`           |
| 10 | blast radius    | draining every target host would exceed max_drained_fraction                                                            | `DENY_BLAST_RADIUS`         |
| 11 | capacity floor  | would leave fewer than min_active_per_role active hosts of a role                                                       | `DENY_ROLE_CAPACITY_FLOOR`  |
| 12 | canary-first    | a runbook proposed against >= fleet_fraction of the fleet must verify on a canary first                                 | `DENY_CANARY_PENDING`       |
| 13 | approval        | DESTRUCTIVE / DISRUPTIVE tier, or any protected-role target: ask the approver pools                                     | `APPROVAL_DESTRUCTIVE_TIER` |
| 14 | allow           | REVERSIBLE on unprotected hosts (or DISRUPTIVE in a maintenance window)                                                 | `ALLOW_REVERSIBLE`          |

## Approvals

A `NEEDS_APPROVAL` verdict carries an `ApprovalRequirement`: one or more **pools**, each an N-of-M requirement (N approvals from the listed roles). Every pool must be filled by *distinct* approvers (matching, not greedy), so a destructive change on a protected host needs the destructive pool **and** the protected pool filled by different people. Any single rejection rejects the request. Unanswered requests page after `escalation.page_after_ticks` and expire after `escalation.expire_after_ticks`. A policy whose stacked pools could never be filled is rejected at load.

## Bundled policies

| policy       | drain cap | cooldown | actions/tick | protected roles                            | destructive approvals | canary                  | freeze | maintenance window | deny-list                                            |
|:-------------|----------:|---------:|-------------:|:-------------------------------------------|:----------------------|:------------------------|:-------|:-------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------|
| `canary`     |       15% |        5 |            8 | db-primary, validator                      | 2 of 2                | 3% of fleet / 1 canary  | -      | yes                | decommission_host                                    |
| `default`    |       10% |        5 |            3 | db-primary, validator                      | 2 of 2                | 5% of fleet / 1 canary  | -      | -                  | decommission_host                                    |
| `freeze`     |       10% |        5 |            3 | db-primary, validator                      | 2 of 2                | 5% of fleet / 1 canary  | yes    | yes                | decommission_host                                    |
| `permissive` |       25% |        3 |            6 | db-primary                                 | 1 of 2                | 10% of fleet / 2 canary | -      | yes                | decommission_host                                    |
| `strict`     |        5% |       10 |            1 | db-primary, db-replica, ingress, validator | 2 of 3                | 3% of fleet / 1 canary  | -      | -                  | decommission_host, failover_db_primary, reimage_host |

- `canary`: Rollout posture: any runbook proposed against 3% of the fleet becomes a campaign that must prove itself on one host first.
- `default`: Production posture: reversible actions auto-run on unprotected hosts, everything else waits for humans.
- `freeze`: Release freeze: only REVERSIBLE runbooks may run; a weekly maintenance window re-opens disruptive work in dc1.
- `permissive`: Faster remediation: wider blast radius, a standing maintenance window for disruptive actions, single approver for destructive ones.
- `strict`: Regulated posture: tight blast radius, 2-of-3 approvals for destructive work, one action per tick, per-DC quotas.

Copy one from `src/fleetgate/data/policies/` and pass it with `--policy path.json`; unspecified keys take the defaults. Show what a policy does with `fleetgate policies NAME`.

## Policy file keys

| key                    | meaning                                                                                              |
|:-----------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `name`                 | lower-case id                                                                                        |
| `protected_roles`      | roles whose hosts always need the protected pool                                                     |
| `max_drained_fraction` | blast-radius cap (fraction of the fleet drained or decommissioned)                                   |
| `cooldown_ticks`       | anti-flapping delay per (host, runbook)                                                              |
| `max_actions_per_tick` | per-tick action budget                                                                               |
| `deny_list`            | runbooks that never run                                                                              |
| `freeze_windows`       | `{start, end, repeat_every?, allow_tiers, label}` tick windows                                       |
| `maintenance_windows`  | `{start, end, repeat_every?, dcs, label}`: DISRUPTIVE on unprotected hosts needs no human inside one |
| `quotas`               | `{window_ticks, per_role, per_dc}` action counts                                                     |
| `approvals`            | `DESTRUCTIVE` / `DISRUPTIVE` / `protected`: `{required, roles}` pools                                |
| `escalation`           | `page_after_ticks`, `expire_after_ticks`                                                             |
| `rate_limits`          | `{runbook: {max, window_ticks}}`                                                                     |
| `canary`               | `{enabled, fleet_fraction, window_ticks, canary_count}`                                              |
| `min_active_per_role`  | capacity floors                                                                                      |

## Reason codes

The prefix is the decision family: `DENY_*`, `APPROVAL_*` (needs approval), `ALLOW_*`. Look one up with `fleetgate explain CODE`.

| code                        | decision       | meaning                                                                                                                                                                                      | fix                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|:----------------------------|:---------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `DENY_UNKNOWN_RUNBOOK`      | DENY           | The proposed runbook id is not in the catalogue. Matching is exact: no trimming, case-folding or Unicode normalisation, so 'drain_host ' and a Cyrillic-'a' lookalike are different strings. | Use an id from `fleetgate runbooks`. If an LLM planner produced it, read the 'plan_filtered' audit entry; fix the prompt or switch to the heuristic planner. Never loosen the matching.                  |
| `DENY_UNKNOWN_HOST`         | DENY           | The host id is not in the fleet (typo, spoofed or stale id).                                                                                                                                 | Check the host exists (`fleetgate simulate --json` lists hosts in incidents); for LLM plans the host must also be inside the incident's scope.                                                           |
| `DENY_LISTED_RUNBOOK`       | DENY           | The runbook is on the policy's deny_list, so it can never run under this policy, with or without approval.                                                                                   | Pick another runbook, or edit deny_list in your policy file (bundled policies are read-only references: copy one and pass it with --policy).                                                             |
| `DENY_FREEZE_WINDOW`        | DENY           | A change freeze is active and this runbook's tier is not in the window's allow_tiers.                                                                                                        | Wait for the window to end, or define a maintenance window for the datacenter (re-opens DISRUPTIVE work on unprotected hosts only; DESTRUCTIVE work stays frozen).                                       |
| `DENY_PRECONDITION_FAILED`  | DENY           | A precondition of the runbook does not hold (host_drained, ticket_open, bmc_reachable, ssh_reachable, ...). The verdict's reason lists exactly which.                                        | Run the prerequisite steps first (drain_host, open_ticket) and keep the playbook order; for bmc/ssh preconditions the host's management path is down: reset_bmc or escalate.                             |
| `DENY_COOLDOWN`             | DENY           | The same runbook already ran on this host within cooldown_ticks (anti-flapping).                                                                                                             | Wait it out (the orchestrator retries automatically for up to 20 ticks) or lower cooldown_ticks. Repeated hits mean a playbook is looping.                                                               |
| `DENY_TICK_BUDGET`          | DENY           | max_actions_per_tick actions have already executed this tick.                                                                                                                                | Nothing to fix: the step retries next tick. Raise max_actions_per_tick if incident backlogs are long.                                                                                                    |
| `DENY_RATE_LIMIT`           | DENY           | The runbook hit its rate_limits entry (max executions per window across the fleet).                                                                                                          | Wait for the window to slide, or raise the limit for that runbook.                                                                                                                                       |
| `DENY_QUOTA_ROLE`           | DENY           | Too many actions on hosts of this role inside the quota window.                                                                                                                              | Wait, or raise quotas.per_role for the role. Quotas exist so one noisy incident cannot churn the primaries.                                                                                              |
| `DENY_QUOTA_DC`             | DENY           | Too many actions in this datacenter inside the quota window.                                                                                                                                 | Wait, or raise quotas.per_dc for the datacenter.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `DENY_BLAST_RADIUS`         | DENY           | Draining would push the drained fraction of the fleet above max_drained_fraction.                                                                                                            | Return repaired hosts (undrain_host / restore_rack), add spare capacity (see the CapacityAgent report), or raise max_drained_fraction in a copy of the policy. The plan is stopped and a human is paged. |
| `DENY_ROLE_CAPACITY_FLOOR`  | DENY           | The action would leave fewer active hosts of a role than min_active_per_role (e.g. the last db-primary).                                                                                     | Add a spare host of that role first, or lower the floor in your policy. The fault stays open and a human is paged.                                                                                       |
| `DENY_CANARY_PENDING`       | DENY           | This runbook is being proposed against a large part of the fleet (a campaign): one canary host must run it and pass verification before the rest.                                            | Nothing to fix: the step waits (up to 20 ticks) for the canary's verification.                                                                                                                           |
| `DENY_CANARY_FAILED`        | DENY           | The campaign's canary failed verification, so the whole campaign is frozen for canary.window_ticks.                                                                                          | Fix the runbook or its probe, or wait for the window; look at the 'verify' audit entry of the canary.                                                                                                    |
| `DENY_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT`     | DENY           | Nobody answered the approval request within expire_after_ticks.                                                                                                                              | Check approver coverage (page_after_ticks paged someone), then re-run; raise escalation.expire_after_ticks if your humans are slower.                                                                    |
| `DENY_APPROVAL_REJECTED`    | DENY           | An approver said no. Any single rejection rejects the request, and approval never overrides a DENY.                                                                                          | Read the approval note in the audit log; fix the plan, not the policy.                                                                                                                                   |
| `DENY_INTERNAL_ERROR`       | DENY           | The gate raised while evaluating (malformed input, a bug). It fails closed.                                                                                                                  | Read the reason text; this should not happen with well-formed input, so please report it.                                                                                                                |
| `APPROVAL_DESTRUCTIVE_TIER` | NEEDS_APPROVAL | The runbook is DESTRUCTIVE (irreversible or data-losing): it needs the DESTRUCTIVE approver pool.                                                                                            | Approve it (N-of-M from the pool in approvals.DESTRUCTIVE), or deny it.                                                                                                                                  |
| `APPROVAL_DISRUPTIVE_TIER`  | NEEDS_APPROVAL | The runbook is DISRUPTIVE (reboots, rebuilds): it needs the DISRUPTIVE approver pool unless a maintenance window covers the datacenter.                                                      | Approve it, or add a maintenance window to the policy.                                                                                                                                                   |
| `APPROVAL_PROTECTED_ROLE`   | NEEDS_APPROVAL | The action touches a host with a protected role (db-primary, validator, ...), including every host of a rack-wide action.                                                                    | Approve it from the protected pool (stacks with the tier's pool, filled by different people).                                                                                                            |
| `ALLOW_MAINTENANCE_WINDOW`  | ALLOW          | ALLOW: a DISRUPTIVE runbook on unprotected hosts inside a maintenance window needs no human.                                                                                                 | Nothing to fix.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `ALLOW_CANARY`              | ALLOW          | ALLOW: this host is the canary for a fleet-wide campaign.                                                                                                                                    | Nothing to fix.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `ALLOW_REVERSIBLE`          | ALLOW          | ALLOW: a REVERSIBLE runbook on unprotected hosts, within every limit.                                                                                                                        | Nothing to fix.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
